name: Arq Backup
summary: Arq is a backup app for Mac and Windows sold as a $59.99 license per computer with no storage included, so backups go to a cloud account, NAS, SFTP server or external drive the buyer already pays for. Plans run hourly or daily, use filesystem snapshots, and encrypt data before it leaves the computer.

facts.text: Arq's home page says it can back up hourly or daily, and can be blocked on specific Wi-Fi networks or on battery power.
By default Arq backs up from an APFS snapshot on macOS or a VSS snapshot on Windows, so each backup reflects one moment in time.
A backup plan can thin backup records as they age, keeping hourly, daily, weekly and monthly records for set periods.
When a password is chosen for a plan, Arq encrypts data before sending it and the password never leaves the computer.
Its product page offers a 30-day free trial and states that no storage is included.

plans.name: Arq license
plans.notes: App only, no storage included. The pricing page does not state a billing period, and one page labels it a license.

hiddenCosts: Storage is bought separately from the provider the buyer chooses, such as a cloud account, NAS or SFTP server.
